newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open lower on Dow's fall.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open lower on Dow's fall.

text.p: Singapore shares opened lower on Monday with sentiment depressed by Wall Street's fall last week, brokers said.
"The Dow's bad performance has definitely contributed to the market's cautious opening this morning," one said.
"Apart from the Dow's weakness, most local investors and foreign funds are staying away because there is no fresh news," another broker said.
The trade was slow and volume small.
After about 50 minutes of trade, the key Straits Times Industrials Index was 6.90 points down at 2,146.64.
Volume was a mere 8.97 million shares. The broader market was mixed with decliners leading rises by 44 to 34.
C. K. Tang, DBS bank and Far East Levingston were major gainers, up between Singapore $0.90 and S$0.50.
Leading losers included Metro Holdings, Jurong Shipyard and DBS Bank Foreign, down by between S$0.21 and S$0.20.

Brokers said the market ws untroubled by the fracas over Jardine Fleming Investment, fined over irregularities in trades. "Jardine's shares have not been affected and there is no impact in the market," said John Yap of Kay Hian James Capel said.
